quarterly_data.signal: CCO Samantha Pearce on the first-line GEA launch of Ziihera: Jazz will report Ziihera revenues quarterly as the best measure of the launch, and with BTC already at more than 50% share, growth from here will be driven by GEA uptake. Launch communication will focus on the triplet regimen, which she called the most appropriate choice given more than 2 years overall survival benefit and use for both PD-L1 positive and PD-L1 negative patients ('probably the first time' - company claim), with the doublet available for patients for whom an immunotherapy is not appropriate. Drawing on GPO contracting experience in the community setting, she does not anticipate significant adoption differences between Medicare and commercial patients. GEA represents 'a sizable proportion' of the $3 billion-$5 billion peak, breast cancer is one of the largest tumor types longer term, and she said Ziihera 'can represent a new standard of care for all HER2 expressing cancers.'
quarterly_data.figure: GEA a sizable proportion of the $3 billion-$5 billion Ziihera peak; BTC share more than 50%

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Samantha Pearce on Epidiolex: the remaining in-label opportunity is particularly the adult long-term care segment, where many LGS patients do not yet have a definitive diagnosis, so Jazz has invested in tools that help physicians diagnose LGS; enrollment in JazzCares extends persistency. She expects the capsule formulation to bring both some conversion of oral-solution patients and incremental growth in the adult segment, without being specific, and said access 'has always been very strong for Epidiolex.' She sized the new populations of the four Epidiolex studies: 'about 120,000 to 150,000 U.S. patients' in the phase III DEE segment and JME 'around about 60,000 U.S. patients'; the JME study uses the capsule formulation.
quarterly_data.figure: DEE about 120,000 to 150,000 U.S. patients; JME around about 60,000 U.S. patients

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Samantha Pearce on XYWAV: roughly two-thirds of net patient adds over the last few quarters have come from idiopathic hypersomnia, where XYWAV 'remains the only licensed product', and the undiagnosed prevalent population could be significantly larger than the diagnosed base. On orexins, Jazz does not yet know how they will be priced or whether payers will support combination therapy; it does not anticipate the stable XYWAV base being switched to an orexin, but 'we may, in time, see some impact there on the pace with which we add patients onto the Xywav.'
quarterly_data.figure: roughly two-thirds of XYWAV net patient adds from IH

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Samantha Pearce on the Actio ABS-1230 KCNT1 epilepsy asset (deal still to close): around 2,500 U.S. patients are diagnosed with KCNT1 epilepsy and prevalence is similar outside the U.S., making it 'an exciting global opportunity for Jazz'; testing is already reflexive for children with epilepsy, and patients can have potentially 100 or so seizures a day. Jazz executive John said Jazz is 'seeing a lot of substrate, especially in epilepsy and oncology', has the balance-sheet capacity for more deals, sets no limits on geography in sourcing, and would fully maximize any asset with broader-than-rare potential, as with Ziihera.
quarterly_data.figure: around 2,500 U.S. KCNT1 epilepsy patients; similar prevalence outside the U.S.

quarterly_data.signal: Jazz executive John: Jazz is 'leaning very heavily' into AI to increase efficiency, with company-wide AI utilization goals and specific use cases in finance, commercial and clinical functions. CCO Samantha Pearce said Jazz set up a new customer-experience part of its commercial organization that uses data, AI and predictive algorithms to identify patients and those at risk of dropping off treatment - for XYWAV, predicting when patients may fall off therapy so patient support programs can intervene, and for Ziihera, understanding when and where GEA patients are diagnosed in a fragmented community setting and feeding next best actions to the sales teams.
